content.comment_body: Hello, I'm facing an issue with two [product_name] units linked via a shielded ethernet cable ([company_name], 2 meters long). Occasionally, both units' LAN indicators turn off for about one second before returning to normal. This mainly happens when the crane in which the [product_name] is installed is in operation. It seems like both the master and the slave units experience this LAN reset intermittently. Hoping for some advice. Thanks.
The earth cable is connected to both [product_name] units. The LAN light goes completely off for one second.
The LAN LED should remain illuminated, either green or orange. If it's not lit, it suggests the ethernet cable isn't connected or the [product_name] isn't receiving power.

1) Can you successfully connect your PC to the [product_name] using this cable? Test both units for PC connectivity. 2) What are the IP addresses assigned to each [product_name] unit? 3) How are these [product_name] units programmed currently?
What does this have to do with the LAN LED going off?

"The LAN LED should always be on, green or orange. If it's not lit, it means the ethernet cable isn't plugged in or there is no power supply." I am aware of that, and there is never any power loss; it is just the LAN connection that drops intermittently.
If the connection only drops occasionally, the LAN LED typically switches between green and orange. However, one of these colors should always be visible.

1. The units work fine most of the time; it's just that sometimes the LAN drops. 2. The IP addresses used are 192.168.000.002 and 192.168.000.003. 3. Programming-wise, there is a master and a slave; each has two expansion modules.
I understand what you mean—if I unplug the LAN cable, the LAN light turns off. Maybe there's a very brief voltage loss to the unit?

As said before, the LAN cable is always connected. The [product_name]'s display never goes dark, and the expansion module's green LED stays on even when the LAN light is off. Do you still think this indicates a power loss? Perhaps if the power drops for just 0.1 seconds, the unit's display doesn't turn off, but the LAN does?

Try connecting only one [product_name] unit to the earth cable. I have some questions regarding the crane control: What supply voltage do the [product_name] units use? Is there a frequency converter in the control, or are the motors directly switched with contactors? What type of motors are installed? It could be a shielding problem due to the controller. Faulty or missing noise filters and high switching currents are frequent causes of these issues. [user_name] (Translated with Google)

The RUN/STOP LED on the expansion module is unrelated to the LAN LED on the main module. They serve different purposes. You now mention that the LAN LED does not go off. Can you clarify: does the LAN LED stay on in either green or orange, or does it go out for a second?

Hi, I'll try connecting just one unit to earth next time. One [product_name] uses 24 VDC, while the other runs on 230V. There's no frequency converter, just contactors. The crane motors use different contactors for up/down movement, and the LAN light tends to go off when the motors are running up or down. There's no noise filter installed; high current switching might be causing these disruptions.

What I meant was that the [product_name]'s display does not go dark when the LAN light goes off. Normally, the LAN light is green or orange while the unit operates, but occasionally, the LAN light turns off for one second, while the display and run/stop LEDs remain on.

I've identified two scenarios when the LAN LED isn't lit: 1) The ethernet cable is not plugged into the [product_name]. If the other end of the cable isn't connected, the LAN LED shows orange. 2) The [product_name] lacks a power supply. In every other case, the LAN LED is green or orange. I am not aware of further possibilities.

As previously mentioned, check for electromagnetic interference and consider connecting only one unit to earth. Also inspect the patch cable connectors for proper connection and clean contacts. Trying a replacement cable, even one without shielding, could help. There might also be issues due to vibrations from crane operation instead of just electromagnetic interference. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report sporadic LAN connection loss between two [product_name] units installed in a crane, indicated by the LAN LED turning off momentarily. The phenomenon is infrequent and does not coincide with overall power loss, and the system typically functions reliably otherwise. This has led to uncertainty regarding the underlying issue, with users suspecting electrical noise or interference related to crane motor operations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect consistent and stable Ethernet connectivity between [product_name] units, with uninterrupted LAN LED indications, regardless of whether nearby heavy equipment is running.
